# Hardening checklist

<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @openverify/docs-tools docs:selfhost` from docs/security/asvs-5.0.0-l2.csv and docs/security/masvs-2.1.0.csv. Do not edit: a test fails when this page differs from a fresh render. -->

The rows of the project's self-assessed checklists whose status is `operator`: what OpenVerify cannot do for you and only the operator of an install can (C277.3). 9 ASVS rows and 1 MASVS row, read from `docs/security/asvs-5.0.0-l2.csv` (OWASP ASVS 5.0.0, Level 2) and `docs/security/masvs-2.1.0.csv` (OWASP MASVS v2.1.0, for the Android SDK's artifacts). Each row gives the requirement's id, never its text: read the requirement in the standard itself. The note is ours, and so is the evidence a reader can follow. A self-assessment is not an audit, and meeting these rows does not make an install meet any standard.

The [requirements](requirements.md#what-only-the-operator-can-do-c2773) page lists the same duties by topic; the checklists' other statuses are summarised in `docs/security/asvs-summary.md`.

## ASVS 5.0.0 Level 2

| Id | Level | What you do (our note) | Evidence | Threats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v5.0.0-4.2.1` | 2 | Message boundaries are Node's strict HTTP parser on each process; the operator's load balancer and ingress must agree on them (one HTTP version end to end, no ambiguous framing). | none | B1-D2 |
| `v5.0.0-12.1.1` | 1 | TLS ends at the operator's ingress or terminator, which sets the versions and suites (the chart's ingress controller, or the operator's proxy on compose). | none | B4-I2 |
| `v5.0.0-12.1.2` | 2 | TLS ends at the operator's ingress or terminator, which sets the versions and suites (the chart's ingress controller, or the operator's proxy on compose). | none | B4-I2 |
| `v5.0.0-12.2.1` | 1 | External TLS and publicly trusted certificates are the operator's; the chart redirects to HTTPS and sends HSTS at its ingress. | none | B4-I2 |
| `v5.0.0-12.2.2` | 1 | External TLS and publicly trusted certificates are the operator's; the chart redirects to HTTPS and sends HSTS at its ingress. | none | B4-I2 |
| `v5.0.0-12.3.4` | 2 | Internal certificates and the CAs each process trusts (OPENVERIFY_*_CA_FILE) are the operator's. | none | B7-I2 |
| `v5.0.0-13.2.5` | 2 | An egress allowlist is the network's: the chart ships default-deny NetworkPolicies, and on compose an egress proxy is the operator's. | `deploy/helm/openverify/tests/c264-networkpolicies_test.yaml` | B10-I3 |
| `v5.0.0-16.4.2` | 2 | Audit entries are append-only in the database (retention deletes only past the environment's setting, measured from the time the caller states, B3-R4); log files and their access are the operator's store. | `packages/db/src/delete-guard.integration.test.ts`, `apps/api/src/services/audit-log.test.ts` | B3-R2, B3-R3 |
| `v5.0.0-16.4.3` | 2 | Shipping logs and audit entries to a separate system is the operator's (G-LOGINV). | `docs/security/logging.md` | B3-R2 |

## MASVS v2.1.0 (the Android SDK)

A library checklist covers the SDK, not the host app it runs in: the host app keeps its own MASVS duties.

| Id | Group | What you do (our note) | Evidence | Threats |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MASVS-NETWORK-2` | MASVS-NETWORK | Pinning is the host app's, through the transport recipe (an OkHttp CertificatePinner with a backup pin), proved by a host test; the SDK ships no pins by design, because each self-hoster has its own certificates (C256.2, decision 41). | `android/openverify-sdk/src/androidHostTest/kotlin/dev/openverify/sdk/CertificatePinningRecipeTest.kt`, `docs/android/integration.md` | B11-S1 |
